EXT.evidence: TargetSpeaker makes brief, task-focused comments (“Are you through with that?”) rather than showing outgoing or energetic sociability.

AGR.evidence: Snaps about mess (“Whose little ball of paper is this?!”) and keeps redoing others’ work (re-fluffing the pillow) to the point another says they’re scared, showing a controlling, less warm tone despite a brief apology.

CON.evidence: Strong focus on order and perfectionism—checking if someone is done, calling out trash, repeatedly fluffing a pillow, and aiming to avoid giving others “ammunition,” indicating careful, organized behavior.

NEU.evidence: Expresses worry about others’ judgment (“don’t wanna give [them] any more ammunition”) and is described as “scaring me… all chaotic and twirly,” showing anxiety and agitation.

OPN.evidence: Cautious and risk-averse stance (avoiding any “ammunition” others could use) and rigid standards about small details (pillow fluffing), suggesting low openness to flexibility.
